optimization_strategy.bottleneck: The CUTLASS 3x3 conv (128x64x16 tile, split_k=1) is 86.6% of steady GPU time (844us/launch on the mid shape = 87% of TF32 peak) and only ~62% of peak on the 2x256x64x64 shape, where it emits just 256 CTAs for 170 SMs (1.5 waves).
optimization_strategy.optimisation method: Specialize the conv configuration per problem shape: instantiate a second, larger CUTLASS tile (128x128x16, warp 64x64x16) for shapes with enough CTAs, and enable serial split-k on the low-CTA shape so the grid covers >=2 full waves. Keep the current 128x64 config as fallback.
optimization_strategy.modification plan:
1. Keep every non-conv kernel (nchw2nhwc_round, weight_krsc_round, gn_partial, gn_finalize, gn_silu_round, gn_silu_add_nchw) and their launch shapes byte-for-byte unchanged; this round touches only the conv path.
2. Add a second instantiation of the existing MakeConv template: `using ConvBig = MakeConv<cutlass::gemm::GemmShape<128,128,16>, cutlass::gemm::GemmShape<64,64,16>, 4>::Op;` and keep `using ConvSmall = MakeConv<GemmShape<128,64,16>, GemmShape<64,32,16>, 4>::Op;`. Both stay ElementA/B = tfloat32_t, ElementAcc = float, Sm80 OpClassTensorOp, InstructionShape 16x8x8, LinearCombination<float,4>, kOptimized, alignment 4/4 (C=K=256 is divisible by 4). Shared memory for ConvBig is (128+128)*16*4B*4 stages = 64KB < 99KB/CTA limit.
3. Extend `run_conv_t` with an `int split_k` parameter and pass it as the last argument of `cutlass::conv::Conv2dProblemSize(..., cutlass::conv::Mode::kCrossCorrelation, split_k)`.
4. In `run_conv_t`, after `get_workspace_size`, zero the workspace before `initialize` (`wsb.zero_()` on the uint8 tensor) — CUTLASS serial split-k (SplitKMode::kSerial, the DefaultConv2dFprop default) uses a semaphore in workspace that must start at 0. For split_k==1 the zeroing is a no-op-sized buffer and costs nothing measurable.
5. Replace the body of `conv3x3` with a compile-time-instantiated, runtime-selected dispatch driven by M = N*H*W and the 170-SM wave criterion (target >= 340 CTAs = 2 full waves):
   - `long M = (long)N*H*W; long ctas_big = ((M+127)/128)*2; long ctas_small = ((M+127)/128)*4;`
   - if (ctas_big >= 340) -> run ConvBig with split_k=1;
   - else if (ctas_small >= 340) -> run ConvSmall with split_k=1;
   - else -> run ConvSmall with `split_k = (int)min(4L, (340 + ctas_small - 1)/ctas_small)` (>=2).
   Concrete outcomes for the scored shapes: 8x64x128 (M=65536) and 4x256x256 (M=262144) -> ConvBig; 1x131x131 (M=17161, ctas_big=270, ctas_small=540) -> ConvSmall split_k=1; 2x64x64 (M=8192, ctas_small=256) -> ConvSmall split_k=2 -> 512 CTAs (3 waves).
6. Make the selection safe: replace the hard `TORCH_CHECK(can_implement...)` for the ConvBig path with a check that, on failure, falls back to ConvSmall split_k=1 with the original TORCH_CHECKs, so no shape can fail to run.
7. Do not change the epilogue (alpha=1, beta=0, output NHWC into y1/y2), the tf32 pre-rounding of activations/weights, or the GN math; numerics must stay within max_atol 0.0028.
8. Verify after building: no local-memory spilling in the conv (registers/thread must stay <= 255 with 0 spill stores) and per-shape timing on all four shapes — if the mid or large shape does not improve with ConvBig, raise the ctas_big threshold so those shapes fall back to ConvSmall rather than regress.
optimization_strategy.evidence: Nsight Systems steady-state table: the CUTLASS ImplicitGemmConvolution is 86.6% of per-forward GPU time (20,264us over 24 launches = 844us/launch); everything else summed is 13.4%, so any non-conv round is Amdahl-capped at 13.4%. At 77.3 GFLOP per conv on the profiled shape, 844us = 91.6 TFLOPS = 87% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak — little headroom there — but the per-shape table shows 2x256x64x64 at only 1.1188x vs 1.2409x for the mid shape; scaling the satellites linearly by pixel count (260us -> 32.5us) leaves ~147us per conv launch = ~65 TFLOPS ~= 62% of peak, and with a 128x64 tile that shape emits only ceil(8192/128)*4 = 256 CTAs for 170 SMs (1.5 waves). Section analysis supports wave quantization as a first-class limiter: NCU's SOLBottleneck OPT on gn_finalize/weight_krsc states 'This kernel grid is too small to fill the available resources on this device, resulting in only 0.25 full waves across all SMs.' Ruled out (secondary): DRAM bandwidth on our own elementwise kernels — gn_silu_add_nchw is at gpu__dram_throughput 88.83% and nchw2nhwc at 86.01%, i.e. already at the memory roof, yet they are 4.6% and 4.3% of steady time; moreover gn_partial moves 67MB in 17.5us = 3.8TB/s, above the 1.79TB/s DRAM peak, proving those passes are L2-resident rather than DRAM-limited, so the memory_bandwidth signature comes from kernels off the critical path. Departure from allowed_methods is deliberate: Own_And_Fuse_Vendor_Operator/KernelFusion can at best delete gn_partial (1.8%) and gn_silu_round (2.1%) — and the SiLU prologue fusion is blocked by the cp.async multistage mainloop — a ~4% ceiling versus the conv-side headroom above; the mechanism I use instead is threadblock-tile/split-k shape dispatch on the dominant operator.
optimization_strategy.expected_metric_change: Conv kernel duration down (mid shape 844us -> <=790us; 2x256x64x64 conv ~147us -> ~115us per launch), global/L2 load bytes per conv output down ~33% on ConvBig shapes ((128+128)*K vs (128+64)*K per tile => 54 -> 36 elements loaded per output, so lts__throughput and l1tex sector counts per conv drop), sm__inst_executed_pipe_tensor rate / achieved TF32 fraction up from ~87% toward >92%, and launch__waves_per_multiprocessor for the small shape up from ~1.5 to ~3.0 via split_k=2. Anti-regression: ConvBig must stay at 64KB shared memory per CTA (<99KB) with zero local-memory spilling requests and registers/thread <=255; the elementwise kernels must keep their current 86-89% DRAM throughput and unchanged launch shapes; if ConvBig or split-k does not beat the incumbent on any scored shape, that shape must fall back to the existing 128x64x16 split_k=1 config so no shape's geomean contribution regresses; the extra workspace zeroing must remain <1us.
